title: Kummer degree functionals in a flat family of possibly nonreduced curves
statement:
Let $c:C\to S$ be separated, flat, of finite presentation and compactifiable between Noetherian schemes, with every nonempty geometric fibre purely one-dimensional [def-weil-pure-dimension] [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-asd-compactifiable]. Let $N\geq1$ be invertible on $S$, let $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$. Use the ordinary etale compact-support functor and $F(1)=F\otimes_R\mu_N$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For a geometric point $\bar s$ and the finite set $I_{\bar s}$ of irreducible components of $C_{\bar s}$, there is a canonical Kummer degree isomorphism
$$H_c^2(C_{\bar s},F_{\bar s}(1))\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I_{\bar s}}F_{\bar s}.$$
It is normalized by degree of line bundles on a proper completion of the reduced components [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; the Kummer Chern class and projective-line normalization have the meaning in [def-amb-p1-trace]. Write $m_i$ for the length of the Artinian local ring of $C_{\bar s}$ at the generic point of component $i$. Under compact-support base change, the functionals $(a_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i m_i a_i$ on the geometric stalks of $R^2c_!c^*F(1)$ are the stalks of a unique $R$-linear sheaf morphism $\delta_{c,F}:R^2c_!c^*F(1)\to F$. This formation is natural in $F$, commutes with change of Noetherian base and with passage from $N'$ to $N$ for $N\mid N'$ with $N'$ invertible on $S$, under $\mu_{N'}\to\mu_N$, $z\mapsto z^{N'/N}$, and restricts along open immersions by extension by zero.

For a separated quasi-finite flat finitely presented $u:C'\to C$, the functionals satisfy $\delta_{cu,F}=\delta_{c,F}\circ R^2c_!(\tau_{u,c^*F(1)})$, where $\tau$ is the weighted sum of [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace]. For a Noetherian scheme $T$ and a separated quasi-finite flat finitely presented $v:S\to T$ with $vc$ compactifiable and $N$ invertible on $T$, they also satisfy $\delta_{vc,F}=\tau_{v,F}\circ v_!(\delta_{c,v^*F})$ for every $R$-module sheaf $F$ on $T$, under the canonical composition identifications. For $c:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ and $F=R_S$, the functional sends the Kummer Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$ to $1$.

Here a Noetherian scheme admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, and a ring is Noetherian when every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: XVIII 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.6 (pp. 485–487), Proposition 1.1.6 and formula 1.1.6.1 (pp. 489–491), Lemmas 1.1.7–1.1.8 and editorial note 4 (p. 491). The degree-two Kummer functional, with generic multiplicities, is the input to 2.9(b); no Stacks tag found for this family statement.

proof.text:
Top tensor comparison, with arbitrary coefficients. Write $R=\mathbf Z/N$. For any separated flat finitely presented compactifiable morphism $a:Z\to S$ of Noetherian schemes with nonempty geometric fibres pure of dimension one and $N$ invertible on $S$, use [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] on a proper compactification and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] on its open part to form the natural projection map
$$F\otimes_R^L Ra_!\mu_N\longrightarrow Ra_!(a^*F\otimes_R\mu_N).$$
For the open part apply the stated sheaf tensor isomorphism termwise to a flat resolution of $F$: restriction is exact, extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and $j_!\mu_N$ is flat since its stalks are either the rank-one free $R$-module or zero. For flatness of $j_!\mu_N$, tensor a short exact sequence with it and take geometric stalks: the resulting sequence is exact because the stalk tensor is either tensor with $R$ or tensor with zero. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks, applied to the kernel and cokernel, then give exactness before taking stalks. The twist is locally free by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Thus this map is an isomorphism by the proper projection formula, without flatness or finite generation of $F$. By [lem-pur-compact-top-localization], $Ra_!\mu_N$ has cohomology only in degrees $0,1,2$ and its stalks compute compact cohomology. Pulling the derived tensor to a geometric stalk is permitted by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply [lem-kun-bounded-tensor-tor-spectral-sequence] there with the second argument $F_{\bar s}[0]$: in total degree two the only term is $\operatorname{Tor}_0(H^2,F_{\bar s})$, since positive Tor lowers degree and $H^q=0$ for $q>2$. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] therefore give the natural sheaf isomorphism
$$\alpha_{a,F}:R^2a_!\mu_N\otimes_R F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^2a_!a^*F(1).$$
The same construction for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives the tensor comparison with every $R$-module $M$.

Geometric Kummer coordinates. First use $F=R$ over an algebraically closed field $k$. The reduction map is a universal homeomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], so [thm-weil-pbc-universalHomeomorphism_pullback] identifies the etale topoi and their cohomology. This also identifies compact supports: in a proper compactification the reduction equivalence carries extension by zero to extension by zero, since the presheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] uses the same open subset and the same restrictions; its cohomology is therefore unchanged. Choose a proper compactification of $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ by [thm-nagata-compactification], which applies because this curve is separated and finite type over the quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Take the closure of $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ there and give it its reduced structure, obtaining a reduced proper completion $\overline Z$. Only components meeting $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ are retained, so this is a pure one-dimensional proper curve with the same generic components. Its boundary is finite by [lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement]. The dense-open isomorphism of [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] identifies $H_c^2(Z_{\mathrm{red}},\mu_N)$ with $H^2(\overline Z,\mu_N)$. The Kummer boundary of [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] identifies this with $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline Z)/N$, and [lem-pur-proper-reduced-curve-multidegree] identifies the latter with $R^I$ by the degrees on its reduced components. These maps define the claimed coordinates; on a proper reduced curve they send every Kummer line-bundle class to its multidegree. For general $M$, tensor with $M$ using Step 1 to get $H_c^2(Z,M(1))\cong\bigoplus_I M$. Define $D_{Z,M}$ to be the coordinate sum weighted by the generic lengths $m_i$.

Dense-open independence and supported generators. Remove the finite component intersections [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite] and shrink each reduced component to a smooth dense open. Such opens exist by [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] and [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open], since $k$ is perfect. Their complements are finite by [lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement]. In each component choose a closed $k$-point $P_i$ in this smooth open by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. It is Cartier there by [lem-sc-point-cartier], hence Cartier in any completion under comparison: away from $P_i$ its ideal is the unit ideal. By [lem-pc-degree-base-change], $\mathcal O(P_i)$ has degree one on this component and degree zero on the others. Its Kummer class is therefore the $i$th coordinate generator by Step 2. The supported Kummer boundary [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] constructs this class already on any neighbourhood of $P_i$, with its canonical trivialization off $P_i$, and is natural under restricting to a smaller such neighbourhood. Applying compact cohomology to $Ri_{P_i*}R\to\mu_N[2]$ produces a class in $H_c^2$; the source has $H_c^0=R$. Extension to a proper completion gives $c_1(\mathcal O(P_i))$ by the relation $c_{P_i,R}u_{P_i}=c_1(\mathcal O(P_i))$ in that node. The composition identifications [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] give the same class through any intermediate open. Hence the extension maps from a common smooth dense open into any two reduced completions preserve every coordinate generator, so preserve the entire degree coordinate isomorphism; those maps are isomorphisms by [lem-pur-compact-top-localization]. This proves independence of completion. For an arbitrary open $W\hookrightarrow Z$, choose the points $P_i$ in $W$ on the components it meets and use the same argument there. Its top extension is the inclusion of just those coordinates. Generic lengths are unchanged on each retained component, so $D_Z\circ\operatorname{ext}=D_W$. Tensoring by Step 1 proves the same statements for every $M$.

Compatibility over a field with a quasi-finite flat source map. Let $u:X\to Y$ be a separated quasi-finite flat finitely presented map of pure one-dimensional curves over the algebraically closed field $k$. By [lem-sbc-flat-locally-quasi-finite-coheight], source generic points have target generic points (both have coheight zero). Remove the finite component intersections and the complements of smooth dense opens in the reductions, using [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite], [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] and [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open]. Remove from the target also the images of the finitely many excluded source points, and restrict the source over the remaining target. These images are closed $k$-points, so the removed sets are finite; the extension maps preserve all top coordinates by Step 3. The remaining reduced source and target are disjoint unions of smooth connected curves, and each source component maps nonconstantly to a target component.

Choose their smooth proper completions by [lem-sc-compactification], then extend each reduced map by [lem-pur-smooth-curve-map-completion] to a finite locally free map $\overline u$. In particular the original reduced map factors as an open immersion into $\overline u^{-1}(Y_{\mathrm{red}})$ followed by the finite locally free map to $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$; it is quasi-finite and flat, so its weighted trace is defined by [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace].

Fix a source component with generic point $\xi$ and its target component with generic point $\eta$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ for the target generic local ring and $B=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ for the source generic local ring, with residue fields $K=\kappa(\eta)$ and $L=\kappa(\xi)$ respectively. Thus the flat local map is $A\to B$, and the reduced function-field extension is $K\to L$. Put $f=\operatorname{length}(A)$, $e=\operatorname{length}(B)$ and $d=\operatorname{length}_B(B/\mathfrak m_A B)$. Tensoring a composition series of $A$ with the flat $A$-module $B$ gives $f$ quotients $B/\mathfrak m_A B$, so $e=fd$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. To check the sheaf trace after reduction, let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $K$. A composition series of the $K$-algebra $Q=B/\mathfrak m_A B$ has $d$ factors $L$. Tensoring with $\Omega$ is exact, so at every point of $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_K\Omega)$ the local length of $Q\otimes_K\Omega$ is $d$ times that of $L\otimes_K\Omega$. The geometric-stalk formula of [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace] therefore identifies the trace for $u$ with $d$ times the reduced trace at the geometric generic target point, including inseparable $L/K$. The equality holds as sheaf maps on the remaining smooth target: the difference sends any local section to a section of the constant sheaf $\mu_N$ vanishing generically; on connected etale neighbourhoods such a section is constant and hence zero.

On the proper completions, [lem-pur-finite-flat-kummer-norm-degree] and the surjective Kummer boundary [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] show that transfer preserves degree. To return to the opens, factor each source inclusion through $\overline u^{-1}(Y_{\mathrm{red}})$. Trace composition and the open-extension counits of [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace] identify the map extended to $\overline Y$ with transfer by $\overline u$ after extension to $\overline X$. Step 3 identifies these extension maps with the degree-coordinate inclusions. Therefore on this source component,
$$f\,D_{Y_{\mathrm{red}},R}\,dH_c^2(\tau_{u_{\mathrm{red}}})=fd\,D_{X_{\mathrm{red}},R}=e\,D_{X_{\mathrm{red}},R}.$$
Sum over source components and tensor with $M$ by Step 1. This proves $D_{X,M}=D_{Y,M}\circ H_c^2(\tau_u)$.

proof.text: Dense relative Cohen–Macaulay locus and local line charts. The fibre Cohen–Macaulay locus $U\subset C$ is open by [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open], and [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] identifies it with the geometric-fibre locus and makes it stable under base change. It contains every fibre generic point: its local ring has dimension zero, the empty regular sequence gives depth at least zero [def-weil-pbc-depth], and [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives the reverse inequality. Since the fibres are pure of dimension one, their complements have dimension zero or are empty by [lem-sbc-nowhere-dense-closed-fibre-dimension]. Thus [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] identifies $R^2(c|_U)_!\mu_N$ with $R^2c_!\mu_N$. On affine opens of $S$, [lem-sbc-cohen-macaulay-flat-quasi-finite-chart] and [lem-sbc-affine-base-flat-quasi-finite-chart-core] supply an open cover of $U$ by flat locally quasi-finite locally finitely presented maps to affine spaces over affine opens of $S$. Their dimensions are one: apply [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] to the pure curve fibres and [lem-sbc-flat-quasi-finite-smooth-local-dimension] to the charts, using [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Shrink each source chart to an affine open. Its target affine space over an affine base is affine too, so the resulting map is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated; being locally quasi-finite and locally finitely presented, it is quasi-finite and finitely presented. Compose with $\mathbf A^1\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1$. These are the required quasi-finite flat line charts. Take finite subcovers since the schemes are Noetherian. All maps used are compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification], so the top-support comparisons apply.

Construct and glue the scalar trace. For a chart $q:V\to\mathbf P^1_{S_0}$ and its projection $p$, define
$$b_q=H^0(t_p)\circ R^2p_!(\tau_{q,\mu_N}):R^2(pq)_!\mu_N\longrightarrow R_{S_0}.$$
Use the normalized trace $t_p$ of [def-amb-p1-trace] and the actual projective-line decomposition [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] with $A=R$. The corner isomorphism and compact-support composition are those of [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] and [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; the quasi-finite functor is exact by [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace]. The projective-line trace on a geometric fibre is the degree map since $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ generates its degree-two group. The compact-support exchange and its pasting compatibility [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], together with the stated base-change compatibilities of $t_p$ and $\tau_q$, identify the stalk of this composite with the composite on the geometric fibre. Step 4 then says that the stalks of $b_q$ are exactly $D_{V_{\bar s},R}$. On overlapping charts their restrictions agree by Step 3. Exactness of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to their equalizer inclusion, detect this equality of sheaf maps. The finite-cover coequalizer of [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] therefore gives a unique map on $R^2(c|_U)_!\mu_N$. Transfer it through the dense-open isomorphism in Step 5 to obtain $\delta_{c,R}$. Its restrictions over affine base opens agree by the same stalk criterion, and hence give a map over $S$. Its stalks are $D_{C_{\bar s},R}$.

Coefficients, uniqueness, and normalization. Define
$$\delta_{c,F}=(\delta_{c,R}\otimes1_F)\circ\alpha_{c,F}^{-1}.$$
Step 1 gives $\alpha$ for every module sheaf $F$. Its stalks identify this map with the weighted sum $\sum_i m_i a_i$, so this is the required map. Naturality in $F$ follows directly from the tensor construction. Any other sheaf map with these stalks is equal to it: the equalizer inclusion is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. For $\mathbf P^1_S$ the map is the trace of [def-amb-p1-trace], since the fibre has one reduced component of multiplicity one; its relation $t_ph=1$ sends $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ to $1$.

Base change and coefficient reduction. Let $S'\to S$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes. The compact-support exchange of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] is defined for all the bounded-below sheaves here, with its composition and pasting compatibilities. The relative CM open of Step 5 pulls back to the relative CM open by [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension]. Pull back the chosen finite cover and line charts. In Step 6, the projective-line trace commutes with base change by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], and $\tau_q$ does by [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace]. Thus each pulled-back local map $b_q$ is exactly the local map for the pulled-back chart. The cover coequalizer and dense-open isomorphism [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] are the extension maps used in the same construction; exact inverse image carries that coequalizer to the pulled-back coequalizer, and the pasting property identifies the extension arrows. Their unique induced maps therefore coincide. The tensor comparison of Step 1 is formed from natural projection maps, so gives the same conclusion for every $F$.

For $N'=dN$, use the diagram of Kummer exact sequences [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] with vertical maps $z\mapsto z^d$ on $\mu_{N'}$, $z\mapsto z^d$ on the first $\mathbf G_m$, and the identity on the second $\mathbf G_m$. Its middle square commutes since $(z^d)^N=z^{N'}$. Its boundary sends $c_{1,N'}(L)$ to $c_{1,N}(L)$; on the coordinates of Step 2 this is reduction $\mathbf Z/N'\to\mathbf Z/N$. The integers $m_i$ do not depend on $N$, so both weighted sums commute with reduction. Step 1 extends this equality to any compatible coefficient map $F'\to F$, in particular to a sheaf $F$ killed by $N$ viewed at both levels. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] give the equality of sheaf maps. No flatness of $\mathbf Z/N$ over $\mathbf Z/N'$ is used.

Source compatibility and open extension. For a separated quasi-finite flat finitely presented morphism $u:C'\to C$, [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace] supplies its exact compact-support functor and trace, stable under base change. Use the top composition comparison [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] and the coherent composition isomorphism [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] to identify the source of the composite. On the stalk at $\bar s$ the asserted equality is exactly Step 4 for $u_{\bar s}$, with coefficients $F_{\bar s}$. It is therefore an equality of sheaf maps by exactness and conservativity of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. If $u$ is an open immersion, its weighted trace is the extension counit, all nonempty point weights being one; alternatively apply Step 3 to the fibre. This proves the open-extension clause, including opens which omit entire fibre components.

A quasi-finite flat map on the base: the multiplicity calculation omitted from the original proof. Let $T$ be Noetherian and $v:S\to T$ separated, quasi-finite, flat and finitely presented, with $vc$ compactifiable and $N$ invertible on $T$; take a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ with algebraically closed field $k$. The finite $k$-scheme $S_{\bar t}$ is the disjoint union of its Artinian local factors $\operatorname{Spec}A_y$; put $n_y=\operatorname{length}(A_y)$. These are precisely the weights in [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace]. On $C_y=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A_y$ its special fibre $C_{y,0}$ is a nilpotent closed subscheme, so it has the same components and compact cohomology by the reduction argument of Step 2. At the generic point $\eta_i$ of a component set $B=\mathcal O_{C_y,\eta_i}$ and let $r_i$ be the length of $B/\mathfrak m_yB$. The map $A_y\to B$ is flat because $c$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Choose a composition series $0=J_0\subset\cdots\subset J_{n_y}=A_y$ with successive quotients $k$. By flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] tensoring gives a filtration $0=J_0B\subset\cdots\subset J_{n_y}B=B$ whose every quotient is $B/\mathfrak m_yB$. Refining each quotient by its composition series shows
$$\operatorname{length}_B(B)=n_y r_i.$$
Consequently $\delta_{vc,F}$ has on this component the weight $n_y r_i$. The other composite first has weight $r_i$, from the geometric fibre of $c$ over $y$, and then weight $n_y$ from $\tau_v$. Both send $(a_{y,i})$ to $\sum_{y,i}n_y r_i a_{y,i}$. This also covers nonreduced fibres of $c$; replacing $r_i$ by $1$ would be incorrect. The composition identification is provided by [lem-pur-compact-top-localization] (outer dimension zero and inner dimension one), using exactness of $v_!$. Thus exactness and conservativity of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] prove the base-composition identity. Empty fibres give empty sums throughout. This completes all clauses.
